title: He had the crown… but lost the heart.
paragraphs: He had the crown… but lost the heart.
That’s the tragedy of Acts of the Apostles 13:22—God removed Saul… and raised up David.

Same throne.
Different spirit.
Let me show you why.

Saul looked the part.
Tall. Impressive. Chosen publicly.

But inside?
Fear-driven. Approval-hungry. Half-obedient.
He obeyed God… selectively.

When God said destroy everything, Saul kept the best.
When confronted, he blamed others.
When exposed, he protected his image.

Saul wanted the kingdom…
without surrender.
David, on the other hand…
Was messy.

He fell into adultery.
He orchestrated death.
He broke hard.
But here’s the line that shakes heaven:
“I have found David… a man after My own heart.”

Not a perfect man.
A responsive man.

When David was confronted, he didn’t defend—
he collapsed in repentance.

No excuses.
No image management.
Just: “I have sinned against the Lord.”
But here’s what we miss…

God is not looking for flawless performance.
He’s looking for a surrendered heart.

Saul resisted correction.
David ran toward it.

Saul preserved reputation.
David pursued restoration.

Saul treated God like a checkbox.
David treated God like oxygen.
And that’s where grace walks in.
Because the real King in this story isn’t David.
It’s Jesus.

The greater David.
The sinless King Saul could never be…
and the Savior David desperately needed.

Where Saul failed and David fell—
Jesus fulfilled.

Perfect obedience.
Perfect surrender.
Perfect sacrifice.

So now the question isn’t:
“Are you more like Saul or David?”
The question is:
Will you come to Jesus when you fail?

If your heart has been drifting…
If you’ve been obeying halfway…
If you’ve been protecting image over intimacy—

God didn’t reject Saul because he sinned.
He rejected him because he refused to return.
David stayed… because he kept coming back.
Come back.

Repent.
Lay it down.
Stop performing. Start surrendering.
Christ is still receiving broken hearts.
And He’s still rewriting stories.
